title: Physical Quantities (Measurable & Non-measurable)
notes:
Definition

Anything that can be measured and expressed in numbers with a definite unit is called a physical quantity. Quantities that cannot be measured — like love, beauty or happiness — are called non-measurable quantities.

Mass can be measured with a balance, length with a ruler and time with a clock, but there is no instrument or unit for measuring beauty. That is why physics deals only with measurable quantities.

Measurable and Non-Measurable Quantities

Measurable quantitiesNon-measurable quantities
Mass, length, time, temperatureLove, beauty, happiness, honesty
Expressed as a number with a unitCannot be expressed in numbers
Measured with instruments (balance, ruler, clock, thermometer)No instrument or unit exists for them

Every physical quantity needs both a number and a unit. Saying "the length is 5" is incomplete — we must say "5 metres", because a physical quantity always carries an associated unit.

Two Classes of Physical Quantities

Physical quantities are divided into two classes:

  • Fundamental quantities — the seven base quantities that are independent of all others (mass, length, time, etc.).
  • Derived quantities — quantities built from fundamental ones (force, velocity, density, etc.).
examples:
**Q1: What are the two types of quantities?**

**Answer:** Measurable quantities and non-measurable quantities.

**Q2: Define physical quantity.**

**Answer:** A quantity that can be measured is called a physical quantity.

**Q3: Into how many classes are physical quantities categorized?**

**Answer:** Two classes: fundamental quantities and derived quantities.

**Q4: Name the two classes of physical quantities.**

**Answer:** Fundamental quantities and derived quantities.

**Q5: Is 'beauty' a physical quantity? Why?**

**Answer:** No, because it cannot be measured numerically.

**Q6: Is 'mass' a physical quantity? Why?**

**Answer:** Yes, because it can be measured using a balance.

**Q7: Give two examples of measurable quantities.**

**Answer:** Length and time.

**Q8: Give two examples of non-measurable quantities.**

**Answer:** Love and honesty.

**Q9: Is temperature measurable?**

**Answer:** Yes, using a thermometer.

**Q10: Can all physical quantities be expressed in numbers with units?**

**Answer:** Yes, that is the defining property of a physical quantity.

**Q11: Why is 'intelligence' not treated as a physical quantity in physics?**

**Answer:** Because it has no standard unit or direct measuring instrument.

**Q12: State whether 'pressure' is measurable.**

**Answer:** Yes, it is measurable and is a physical quantity.

**Q13: State whether 'sadness' is measurable.**

**Answer:** No, it is a non-measurable quantity.

**Q14: What distinguishes a physical quantity from a non-physical one?**

**Answer:** The ability to be measured with a definite unit.

**Q15: Is electric current a physical quantity?**

**Answer:** Yes, it is measurable using an ammeter.

**Q16: Give an example of a quantity that seems physical but is actually subjective.**

**Answer:** Comfort level (depends on perception, not a fixed measurable standard).

**Q17: Which branch of science primarily deals with physical quantities?**

**Answer:** Physics.

**Q18: Can a physical quantity exist without a unit?**

**Answer:** No, every physical quantity must have an associated unit.

**Q19: Is 'luminous intensity' measurable?**

**Answer:** Yes, it is a fundamental physical quantity.

**Q20: What is the opposite category of measurable quantities?**

**Answer:** Non-measurable quantities.

**Q21: Name one derived physical quantity.**

**Answer:** Force (or velocity, area, etc.).

**Q22: Name one fundamental physical quantity.**

**Answer:** Mass (or length, time, etc.).

**Q23: Why must physical quantities be quantified precisely?**

**Answer:** So they can be compared, calculated, and used in laws of physics.

**Q24: Give an example of a quantity that depends on other quantities.**

**Answer:** Density (depends on mass and volume).

**Q25: Is 'volume' fundamental or derived?**

**Answer:** Derived.

**Q26: True or False: All measurable quantities are fundamental.**

**Answer:** False, measurable quantities can be either fundamental or derived.
keyPoints: - **Definition:** A physical quantity is anything that can be measured; it is classed as measurable (physical) or non-measurable (like love, beauty).
